explanation: The std::sort algorithm is a fundamental part of the C++ Standard Library, providing an efficient, in-place sorting mechanism for ranges defined by iterators. It operates on random-access containers such as vectors, lists, or arrays. The sort() algorithm typically implements a variation of quicksort, offering good average-case performance with a complexity of O(n log n). Using iterators, programmers can sort any container that supports iterator access, promoting code reusability and abstraction.
syntax: template <class RandomIt> void sort(RandomIt first, RandomIt last);
